title: KNN transfer with a model-free spectral similarity (fragment + neutral-loss cosine) [amended NL rule]
axis: scoring rule: A0 = z(nf) + 0.25 doc; A1 = A0 + beta * z(knn_cos), knn_cos = similarity-weighted Tanimoto of the candidate to the structures of the query's nearest library spectra under a classic cosine (no learned component)
question: Does an analog search independent of our model (E002 used the model's own embedding and was redundant) add ranking information beyond our model and the documentation prior?
hypothesis: A1 beats A0 on np_c2 (primary) without losing on np_tims.
builds_on: E002; supersedes E003 (archived before any result)

rules.index: the same 1,865,951 training-visible spectra as E002 (asserted free of cell structures)
rules.similarity: cosine of sqrt relative intensity over the 50 most intense peaks; fragment m/z bins of 0.01 Da (+) neutral-loss (precursor - fragment, >= 1.5 Da: excludes the residual precursor peak) bins of 0.01 Da; each block L2-normalised and weighted 1/sqrt(2), so sim = (cos_fragment + cos_loss) / 2

knn.weights: softmax(sim / 0.05) over the union of the molecule's neighbours, pooled by structure (max)

rules.beta_selection: grid {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2}; the beta used on each cell is the best mean MRR on the OTHER cell
rules.secondary_not_in_verdict: A0 + beta z(knn_emb) + beta z(knn_cos) with the same cross-cell beta choice; knn_cos alone; doc + knn_cos
rules.leak_policy: every arm leak-free on every cell, and the index holds no spectrum of a cell structure, else void
rules.consequence: knn_cos_helps -> candidate signal for the pipeline's ranks 2-25 and the first piece of a class-3 analog route
limitations: binned cosine approximates matched-peak cosine (bin edges)
